ledger.failureMode: scaffoldXunitFile always declares the injected fixture as a private field named _fixture (constructor parameter named fixture) and splices the caller's testBody into the generated method unchanged, yet that body is authored against the consuming project's own sibling tests, which may keep the fixture under a different member name (for example fixture, _factory or _app). Only collection and fixtureType can be passed in, so a new xUnit class generated for such a project contains a method body that refers to a member the class does not declare, and the file does not compile.
ledger.evidence: Read lib/spec-writer.js:240-245: the new-class template hard-codes 'private readonly ${fixtureType} _fixture;' and a constructor '(${fixtureType} fixture)' that assigns it; scaffoldXunitFile takes no option to name either (it only reads className, ns, collection, fixtureType, usings). The command's landing step (commands/author-playwright-tests.yaml:226) lists only {collection, fixtureType} as the project-specific inputs for a new xunit file, and the proposal stage tells the author to build the context and page as the project's sibling tests do (agents/playwright-tester.yaml:61, commands/author-playwright-tests.yaml:181), so nothing ties the body's fixture member to _fixture. tests/spec-writer-xunit.test.js uses one body constant written against _fixture for every xUnit case and compares the output with a golden string, so it only exercises the self-consistent case and cannot show whether the generated C# compiles under another naming. I ran a throwaway node snippet against the snapshot: scaffoldNewSpecFile with framework 'xunit', collection 'Pw', fixtureType 'PwFixture' and testBody 'await using var ctx = fixture.NewContext();' printed a class whose only fixture members are the field _fixture (output line 11) and the constructor parameter fixture (line 13), with the method body (line 22) still calling fixture.NewContext(), a name that is not in scope inside the method. An append to an existing class uses that class's own members, so only new xUnit files are affected.
